questionText:
Consider a file of size 4 million bytes being transferred between two hosts connected via a path consisting of three consecutive links of bandwidth 2 Mbps, 500 kbps, and 1 Mbps, respectively. All processing delays and propagation delays are negligible. Assume that there is no other background traffic over the path and no other additional overhead to transfer the file.

Which one of the following is the total time (in seconds) to transfer the file?

Note: $1\text{M}=10^6$, $1\text{k}=10^3$
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

1. Calculate File Size in Bits:
File size $= 4 \text{ million bytes} = 4 \times 10^6 \text{ bytes} = 4 \times 10^6 \times 8 \text{ bits} = 32 \times 10^6 \text{ bits}$.

2. Identify Bottleneck Bandwidth:
The path consists of three links with bandwidths:
- Link 1: $2 \text{ Mbps} = 2 \times 10^6 \text{ bps}$
- Link 2: $500 \text{ kbps} = 0.5 \times 10^6 \text{ bps}$
- Link 3: $1 \text{ Mbps} = 1 \times 10^6 \text{ bps}$

The throughput across the end-to-end path is constrained by the bottleneck link (the link with minimum bandwidth):
$$\text{Bottleneck Bandwidth} = 500 \text{ kbps} = 0.5 \times 10^6 \text{ bps}$$

3. Calculate Total Transfer Time:
$$\text{Total Time} = \frac{\text{File Size}}{\text{Bottleneck Bandwidth}} = \frac{32 \times 10^6 \text{ bits}}{0.5 \times 10^6 \text{ bits/s}} = 64 \text{ seconds}$$

Therefore, the correct option is (B).
